Certainly! Here’s a comprehensive overview of **Beaumont Hamel British Cemetery**:

---

## **Location**
- **Country:** France
- **Region:** Somme department (Hauts-de-France)
- **Nearest Village:** Beaumont-Hamel
- The cemetery is located just north of the village of Beaumont-Hamel.
- It is close to the site of the Battles of the Somme and adjacent to the **Newfoundland Memorial Park**.

---

## **Historical Significance**
- **War burials:** Primarily contains burials from World War I.
- The area witnessed intense fighting during the **Battle of the Somme (1916)**, particularly during the opening day (July 1, 1916) and subsequent months.
- Beaumont-Hamel is especially associated with the tragic losses of the **Newfoundland Regiment** on July 1, 1916.

---

## **Establishment & Use**
- The cemetery was begun in late 1916, after the area was finally captured in November 1916 during the **Battle of the Ancre** (a phase of the Somme Offensive).
- Bodies were brought in from the battlefield, and the cemetery was used by fighting units and field ambulances.

---

## **Layout & Features**
- **Architect:** Designed by Sir Reginald Blomfield.
- The cemetery is rectangular, typical of Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC) cemeteries, and contains a **Cross of Sacrifice**.
- The entrance is marked, and the site is well-tended, featuring uniform headstones and landscaped grounds.

---

## **Burials**
- **Graves:** Contains over **179 Commonwealth burials** of the First World War.
    - **Identified:** Of these, around **135 are identified**.
    - **Unidentified:** The rest are unknown soldiers.
- **Special Memorials:** Several special memorials commemorate soldiers known or believed to be buried among the unknown.

---

## **Notable Facts**
- The cemetery is **distinct** from Hawthorn Ridge Cemetery No. 1 and Hawthorn Ridge Cemetery No. 2, which are nearby and also contain casualties from the same battles.
- Located near several other famous war cemeteries and memorials on the **Somme**.

---

## **Visiting Information**
- **Managed by:** Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC).
- **Year-round access** is permitted.
- Often visited together with the **Newfoundland Memorial Park**, which preserves trenches and battlefield ground.

---

### **References & Further Information**
- **CWGC Official Page:** [CWGC – Beaumont Hamel British Cemetery](https://www.cwgc.org/visit-us/find-cemeteries-memorials/cemetery-details/36300/beaumont-hamel-british-cemetery/)
- **Wikipedia:** [Beaumont-Hamel British Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaumont-Hamel_British_Cemetery)
- **Newfoundland Memorial Park:** [Website](https://www.gov.nl.ca/executive/branch/beaumont-hamel/) (for context about the nearby park)

---

### **Summary Table**

| Feature         | Details                                   |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------|
| Established     | 1916                                      |
| Burials         | 179 (mainly WWI)                          |
| Identified      | ~135                                      |
| Unidentified    | ~44                                       |
| Location        | North of Beaumont-Hamel, Somme, France    |
| Designer        | Sir Reginald Blomfield                    |
| Managed by      | CWGC                                      |
| Notable Nearby  | Newfoundland Memorial Park, Hawthorn Ridge|

---
